**Finding submitted: deviation (INDEMN), fallback-level cure.**

What I found across the document:
- **Article XII (p0128–p0129)** is a one-way indemnity: Licensee defends, indemnifies and holds Licensor harmless, with no reciprocal Licensor obligation.
- **No Licensor indemnity exists anywhere** — Articles VIII, X (confidentiality/non-solicit), XI (injunctive relief, Licensor-side only) and the General Provisions contain none; the only other infringement references (p0048, p0112) are Licensor's IP-enforcement rights and a disclaimer of the implied non-infringement warranty.
- **Article XIII(a)** affirmatively bars any Licensor liability for third-party infringement claims, and **XIII(b)** caps Licensor at one half of amounts paid — i.e. walk-away territory, failing the fallback.

Cure (shortest complete fallback package, validated `ok:true`):
1. New **Article XII-A** after p0129: Licensor IP indemnity for third-party infringement/misappropriation claims, with the customary Licensee-modification, combination and specification exclusions, procure/modify/replace remedies, refund if unavailable, and a super-cap of 3× annual fees.
2. A single surgical edit to p0130 carving Licensor's Article XII-A indemnity out of the (a) infringement liability exclusion and the (b) one-half cap, so the new indemnity is not negated by retained mechanics.

Preferred-level items (defence duty, affiliates, breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct, notice/control/cooperation procedure, narrowing Licensee's indemnity) are noted in the rationale but not drafted, since the fallback is the selected target.
